coastal.title: Coastal water challenges
coastal.subtitle: Communities in Satkhira, Khulna and Bagerhat face connected challenges in accessing safe drinking water.

items.title: Groundwater and arsenic
items.body: Groundwater quality varies by location. Arsenic is a known concern in parts of Bangladesh; test water sources and follow local public-health guidance.

items.title: Salinity in drinking water
items.body: Saline conditions can make reliable drinking-water access difficult, especially in coastal areas. Rainwater harvesting can be one part of a locally appropriate response.

items.title: Electricity and treatment costs
items.body: Some treatment approaches require electricity, maintenance and household investment, which may be difficult to sustain.

items.title: Distance to safe water
items.body: When a safe source is far away, families may face additional time and transport burdens to collect water.

items.title: Shrimp-shell waste
items.body: Shrimp processing can leave shells that are discarded. Reusing suitable shell waste can support a circular-economy approach.

items.title: A complementary response
items.body: Shonjibon is developing an electricity-free filter that helps reduce arsenic, heavy metals and turbidity. It does not remove salinity or disinfect water.

concerns.title: Our concerning issues
concerns.subtitle: The challenges are connected; solutions need to be locally tested and community-led.

items.title: Unsafe drinking water
items.body: Water quality can vary between sources. Testing and locally trusted guidance matter.

items.title: Cost of treatment
items.body: Equipment, energy and maintenance costs can make some treatment options hard to access.

items.title: Shrimp-shell waste
items.body: Discarded shells can create a local waste burden instead of becoming a useful resource.

items.title: Women's livelihood opportunities
items.body: Community-led shell processing and craft work can create opportunities when designed fairly and safely.

items.title: Children and pregnancy
items.body: Children and pregnant people may be more vulnerable to health risks from unsafe water; consult health professionals and local authorities.

items.title: Access to testing
items.body: People need practical access to trustworthy water testing and clear explanations of results.

health.title: Health and water safety
health.subtitle: General information about water-related health concerns. Consult qualified health professionals for personal advice.

items.title: Arsenic exposure
items.body: Long-term exposure to arsenic in drinking water can pose serious health risks. Use tested sources and follow public-health advice.

items.title: Diarrheal disease and cholera
items.body: Unsafe water can contribute to diarrheal illness. Follow local water-treatment and sanitation guidance; seek care for dehydration or severe symptoms.

items.title: Salinity and maternal health
items.body: Drinking-water salinity is a public-health concern in some coastal settings. Pregnant people should discuss individual concerns with a qualified clinician.

items.title: Skin problems
items.body: Skin symptoms can have many causes. A healthcare professional can help identify the cause and recommend treatment.

items.title: Practical safety steps
items.body: Use a tested safe source where available, store drinking water in clean covered containers, and follow local health advisories.

health.doctorBody: Seek medical care for severe or persistent diarrhea, signs of dehydration, concerning skin changes, or any urgent symptoms.
health.disclaimer: This page provides general educational information, not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
